exact_survey_question: Are you the primary income earner in your household? (all branches)
why_classification_uncertain: Being the primary earner is a household ECONOMIC ROLE fact. It does not itself state anything about the respondent's available time, schedule, or ability to attend a programme. This is the task's own worked example of a forbidden inference ('primary household provider does NOT automatically mean cannot attend full-time').
alternative_classifications: INDIVIDUAL_CONTEXT_ONLY (supports explanation, e.g. 'this respondent is the household's main earner'); or FEASIBILITY_OR_CONSTRAINT_CONTEXT but restricted to may_drive=False until corroborated by a direct schedule-preference answer.
risk_if_allowed_to_drive_directly: LLM infers 'primary earner -> needs part-time/short course' without the respondent ever saying so — exactly the prohibited inference pattern named in the task brief.
risk_if_prohibited_from_use: A genuinely time-constrained provider loses a legitimate signal that could have prompted the system to ASK a direct follow-up question about schedule need — but this is a minor loss since the new 5-question intake already asks schedule directly.
scientific_justification: No course dataset field or documented rule converts 'is primary earner' into a schedule/duration constraint. The forthcoming intake questionnaire asks Q3 (weekday/full-time vs weekend/part-time) directly. Using this survey variable to drive scheduling would substitute inference for the respondent's own direct answer.

exact_survey_question: Who mainly determines how you spend your time on a day-to-day basis? (Branch G)
why_classification_uncertain: This is closer to a genuine autonomy statement than primary_earner_status (it directly names who controls the respondent's schedule), but it still does not state a concrete attendance constraint — 'someone else decides my time' does not specify whether that person would permit training attendance.
alternative_classifications: INDIVIDUAL_CONTEXT_ONLY (context/explanation only); or keep as FEASIBILITY_OR_CONSTRAINT_CONTEXT but scope-limited to corroborating evidence only, never a standalone driver.
risk_if_allowed_to_drive_directly: LLM could infer 'someone else controls their time -> exclude from full-time/away-from-home programmes' without the respondent stating that outcome.
risk_if_prohibited_from_use: A real autonomy barrier (e.g. needing a guardian's permission to attend) is not surfaced to ranking, only to explanation — likely an acceptable trade-off given how directly the new intake questionnaire will ask about schedule.
recommended_classification: FEASIBILITY_OR_CONSTRAINT_CONTEXT but may_drive=False (i.e. reclassify to INDIVIDUAL_CONTEXT_ONLY) pending explicit corroboration
scientific_justification: It is a genuine, directly-answered autonomy fact, so it is not a pure proxy — but on its own it does not specify a resulting constraint on any course attribute (schedule, duration, location). It should support explanation and prompt a direct follow-up, not silently move a ranking score.

exact_survey_question: If you were to start working or studying, how much support could you expect from the people around you? (Branch G)
why_classification_uncertain: Every other social-support/network variable in this survey (employment_network_quality, knows_people_in_target_sector, network_helpfulness, labour_market_connection) was classified INDIVIDUAL_CONTEXT_ONLY. support_for_engagement measures the same kind of expected-support construct and was inconsistently placed in the driving-eligible feasibility category.
alternative_classifications: INDIVIDUAL_CONTEXT_ONLY, for consistency with the other social-support variables in this same audit set.
risk_if_allowed_to_drive_directly: Low family/household support could be read by the LLM as a reason to deprioritise a programme, which risks penalising a respondent for their family's attitude rather than their own stated interest or constraint.
risk_if_prohibited_from_use: Minimal — this is a supporting/contextual signal, not a stated preference or hard constraint.
scientific_justification: Consistency with the rest of the social-support/network variable family, all of which were correctly scoped as explanation-only. No direct course attribute exists for 'expected family support.'

exact_survey_question: What is the approximate total monthly income of your household from all sources? (all branches)
why_classification_uncertain: The NYSC course matching dataset (V2, 87 courses) has NO fee, cost, scholarship, or subsidy field. There is currently no course-side attribute that a household-income level could legitimately be matched against. The task's own critical rule names this exact case: 'low household income must NOT automatically mean recommend a shorter course... unless... the catalogue provides the necessary cost/feasibility information.'
alternative_classifications: INDIVIDUAL_CONTEXT_ONLY until a course-cost/subsidy field is added to the catalogue.
risk_if_allowed_to_drive_directly: LLM invents a cost-based justification ('this course is more affordable for a lower-income household') that the catalogue cannot actually support, producing plausible-sounding but fabricated reasoning.
risk_if_prohibited_from_use: None currently — there is no legitimate mechanism to lose, since no catalogue field exists to connect income to.
recommended_classification: INDIVIDUAL_CONTEXT_ONLY (may_drive=False, may_support=True) until a documented course-cost field exists
scientific_justification: Directly matches the task's own critical-rule example. The classification should track catalogue capability, not just whether the respondent answered directly.

exact_survey_question: How many people in your household are currently working for a salary or wage? (all branches)
why_classification_uncertain: A structural household-composition count, not a statement about the respondent's own constraint. Shares the same 'no course-side cost mechanism' problem as household_income, of which it is a component.
alternative_classifications: INDIVIDUAL_CONTEXT_ONLY.
risk_if_allowed_to_drive_directly: Same fabricated-cost-reasoning risk as household_income, one step further removed from any respondent statement.
risk_if_prohibited_from_use: None currently.
scientific_justification: Same reasoning as household_income; this is one of its structural components, not an independent constraint statement.

exact_survey_question: How many people in your household are currently without work and actively looking for a job? (all branches)
why_classification_uncertain: Same issue as household_workers — a structural household-composition count with no course-side mechanism to connect to.
alternative_classifications: INDIVIDUAL_CONTEXT_ONLY.
risk_if_allowed_to_drive_directly: Same fabricated-cost/urgency-reasoning risk as household_income.
risk_if_prohibited_from_use: None currently.
scientific_justification: Same reasoning as household_income.

exact_survey_question: Currently, where does most of your money come from? (all branches)
why_classification_uncertain: States WHERE money comes from (parents, own job, grant, etc.), not a stated forward constraint on programme choice; no catalogue-side cost/funding-eligibility field exists to connect it to.
alternative_classifications: INDIVIDUAL_CONTEXT_ONLY.
risk_if_allowed_to_drive_directly: LLM could infer funding-eligibility ('funded by parents, so cost is not a concern') that the catalogue cannot verify.
risk_if_prohibited_from_use: None currently.
scientific_justification: Same catalogue-capability reasoning as household_income.

exact_survey_question: How is your current education mainly funded? (Branch D)
why_classification_uncertain: Describes how CURRENT education is funded — a historical/current fact, not a forward statement about willingness or ability to pay for a NEW NYSC course. No catalogue cost field exists.
alternative_classifications: EDUCATION_AND_EXPERIENCE_CONTEXT or INDIVIDUAL_CONTEXT_ONLY.
risk_if_allowed_to_drive_directly: Same fabricated-cost-reasoning risk as household_income, plus an unjustified time-transfer (current funding arrangement assumed to carry forward to a different programme).
risk_if_prohibited_from_use: None currently.
scientific_justification: No catalogue-side cost mechanism, and the fact describes a different (current) programme, not the one being recommended.

exact_survey_question: On average, what is your total income from work per month? (Branch F)
why_classification_uncertain: Same catalogue-capability gap as household_income — no course-cost field exists to legitimately connect a personal income band to.
alternative_classifications: INDIVIDUAL_CONTEXT_ONLY.
risk_if_allowed_to_drive_directly: Same fabricated-cost-reasoning risk as household_income.
risk_if_prohibited_from_use: None currently.
scientific_justification: Same reasoning as household_income.

exact_survey_question: Who paid for the training you received for your current job? (Branch F, conditional on received_training)
why_classification_uncertain: A historical fact about a PAST training episode's funding, not a forward-looking constraint or preference about a NEW course. Originally mis-classified as a live financial constraint.
alternative_classifications: EDUCATION_AND_EXPERIENCE_CONTEXT (training-history detail, consistent with training_provider/training_duration/training_type_received, which were all correctly classified there).
risk_if_allowed_to_drive_directly: LLM could wrongly assume the same funding source would apply to a new NYSC course.
risk_if_prohibited_from_use: None — this is purely historical context.
scientific_justification: Corrects an inconsistency: this variable's three sibling variables (training_provider, training_duration, training_type_received) were already correctly classified as non-driving experience context; who_paid_training should match them.

exact_survey_question: Is there a minimum monthly income below which you would not accept a job? (Branch E)
why_classification_uncertain: States a JOB-acceptance wage floor. No NYSC course in the V2 catalogue has an associated wage-outcome field, so there is nothing for this to be legitimately matched against for COURSE selection.
alternative_classifications: INDIVIDUAL_CONTEXT_ONLY (still meaningful for explaining employment-search behaviour, just not course-relevant).
risk_if_allowed_to_drive_directly: LLM could invent an unsupported wage-outcome claim about a course ('this course leads to jobs meeting your minimum wage'), which the catalogue cannot verify.
risk_if_prohibited_from_use: None for course matching; this variable is about job search, not training selection.
scientific_justification: Topic mismatch: a job-acceptance wage condition does not map to any documented course attribute.

exact_survey_question: What is the approximate minimum monthly income you would need to accept a job? (Branch E, conditional on has_minimum_wage)
why_classification_uncertain: Same topic-mismatch issue as has_minimum_wage.
alternative_classifications: INDIVIDUAL_CONTEXT_ONLY.
risk_if_allowed_to_drive_directly: Same as has_minimum_wage.
risk_if_prohibited_from_use: None for course matching.
scientific_justification: Same reasoning as has_minimum_wage.

exact_survey_question: How urgently do you need to start earning income? (Branch E)
why_classification_uncertain: Unlike the other income variables, this DOES map to a real, documented course attribute — duration_months in the V2 catalogue — but only if the RAG stage builds an explicit, documented rule ('high urgency -> prefer shorter duration_months'). Left implicit, it is exactly the kind of plausible-but-unverified reasoning the critical rule prohibits.
alternative_classifications: Keep as FEASIBILITY_OR_CONSTRAINT_CONTEXT but require the future scoring design to state the urgency-to-duration mapping explicitly and show its provenance in any generated explanation (never silently).
risk_if_allowed_to_drive_directly: Without an explicit documented rule, the LLM could apply an unstated urgency-to-duration weighting inconsistently across respondents.
risk_if_prohibited_from_use: A genuinely time-urgent respondent loses a legitimate, directly-stated signal that could sensibly favour shorter courses.
recommended_classification: FEASIBILITY_OR_CONSTRAINT_CONTEXT, may_drive=True, but ONLY via an explicit documented duration-preference rule built at the scoring stage — not an ad hoc LLM inference
scientific_justification: This is the one income-family variable with both a direct respondent statement AND a real matching catalogue field (duration_months), so it should remain drive-eligible in principle — the risk is entirely about HOW it is used, not WHETHER.

exact_survey_question: Do you have any children? (all branches)
why_classification_uncertain: A genuine care-responsibility fact (explicitly named as a legitimate example in the task brief), but it does not itself state a schedule/duration constraint — the same 'does not automatically mean X' pattern the task's own example targets (analogous to primary_earner_status).
alternative_classifications: Keep as FEASIBILITY_OR_CONSTRAINT_CONTEXT but restrict to a corroborating/soft-flag role, never a standalone schedule filter; or downgrade to INDIVIDUAL_CONTEXT_ONLY entirely.
risk_if_allowed_to_drive_directly: LLM auto-infers 'has children -> needs part-time/weekend' without the respondent ever stating a schedule preference — the task's own named failure pattern.
risk_if_prohibited_from_use: A real care-driven schedule need is not surfaced to ranking — acceptable because the new 5-question intake asks schedule (Q3) directly, and has_children can still support explanation and prompt that direct question.
recommended_classification: FEASIBILITY_OR_CONSTRAINT_CONTEXT retained, but may_drive=False (effectively INDIVIDUAL_CONTEXT_ONLY) unless/until corroborated by the respondent's own direct schedule answer
scientific_justification: Matches the task's explicit critical-rule pattern almost exactly. The direct schedule answer (from the new intake questionnaire) is the legitimate driver; this variable should support and corroborate it, not substitute for it.

exact_survey_question: How many children do you have? (all branches, conditional on has_children)
why_classification_uncertain: Same reasoning as has_children; a count does not add a stated constraint beyond the yes/no fact.
alternative_classifications: Same as has_children.
risk_if_allowed_to_drive_directly: Same as has_children, with an added risk of implying 'more children = more constrained,' an unstated and unverified scaling assumption.
risk_if_prohibited_from_use: Same as has_children.
recommended_classification: FEASIBILITY_OR_CONSTRAINT_CONTEXT retained, but may_drive=False, matching has_children
scientific_justification: Same reasoning as has_children.

exact_survey_question: How many hours per week do you usually work at your main job? (Branch F)
why_classification_uncertain: Describes CURRENT job hours, not a stated future availability for TRAINING attendance. The new 5-question intake asks schedule preference (Q3: weekday/full-time vs weekend/part-time) directly for the NEW course — using historical job-hours data to drive that same decision would be an unstated proxy inference, and the two commitments (an existing job vs a new course) are not interchangeable.
alternative_classifications: EDUCATION_AND_EXPERIENCE_CONTEXT or INDIVIDUAL_CONTEXT_ONLY (context/explanation only).
risk_if_allowed_to_drive_directly: LLM infers 'works 40 hrs/week -> can only attend part-time/weekend training' without the respondent ever being asked about training availability specifically.
risk_if_prohibited_from_use: None of substance — the direct Q3 schedule answer from the new intake is the legitimate driver going forward.
scientific_justification: Topic mismatch between an existing-job-hours fact and a new-course-schedule decision; a direct, purpose-built schedule question already exists in the approved intake design and should be the sole driver.

exact_survey_question: Last week, how many hours did you actually work at your main job? (Branch F)
why_classification_uncertain: Same reasoning as usual_hours_per_week, and additionally a single-week snapshot that may not represent the respondent's typical availability at all.
alternative_classifications: INDIVIDUAL_CONTEXT_ONLY.
risk_if_allowed_to_drive_directly: Same as usual_hours_per_week, compounded by single-week volatility.
risk_if_prohibited_from_use: None of substance.
scientific_justification: Same reasoning as usual_hours_per_week.

exact_survey_question: If you could choose regarding your work hours and income, which would you prefer? (Branch F)
why_classification_uncertain: This IS a genuine, directly-stated preference (correctly classified as category A in that narrow sense), but it is a preference about the respondent's CURRENT JOB's hours/income trade-off, not about a NEW training programme's schedule. Applying a job-hours preference directly to course-schedule ranking is a topic-mismatch, not a missingness or proxy problem.
alternative_classifications: Keep as DIRECT_PREFERENCE_OR_INTENT for explanation purposes (e.g. 'currently prefers to keep hours the same'), but do not let it drive course-schedule ranking.
risk_if_allowed_to_drive_directly: LLM treats a job-hours preference as if it were a training-schedule preference, producing a plausible-sounding but topically unjustified schedule match.
risk_if_prohibited_from_use: None of substance — the new intake's direct schedule question is the correct driver for course scheduling.
recommended_classification: DIRECT_PREFERENCE_OR_INTENT retained for classification honesty, but may_drive=False specifically for course-schedule ranking (support/explanation only)
scientific_justification: The category label (A) is correct for what the variable IS; the drive-eligibility flag is wrong because the preference's SUBJECT (current job) does not match the TARGET decision (new course schedule).

exact_survey_question: If a job opportunity had arisen last week, would you have been able to start work? (Branch E)
why_classification_uncertain: Measures availability to start a JOB, not availability to attend TRAINING — a different commitment type and timeframe (immediate, one-off, last week) than course enrolment.
alternative_classifications: INDIVIDUAL_CONTEXT_ONLY.
risk_if_allowed_to_drive_directly: LLM conflates 'able to start a job last week' with 'able to attend training now,' an unjustified topic transfer.
risk_if_prohibited_from_use: None of substance for course matching.
scientific_justification: Topic and timeframe mismatch with the target decision (course enrolment).

exact_survey_question: Would you consider relocating to find work? (Branch E)
why_classification_uncertain: The V2 course catalogue has no district/location field for any of the 87 courses, so there is currently no course-side attribute this could be legitimately matched against for course selection.
alternative_classifications: INDIVIDUAL_CONTEXT_ONLY until course location data exists in the catalogue.
risk_if_allowed_to_drive_directly: LLM could claim a course is or is not geographically feasible without any actual location data to check against.
risk_if_prohibited_from_use: None currently — no legitimate mechanism exists to lose.
recommended_classification: INDIVIDUAL_CONTEXT_ONLY (may_drive=False, may_support=True) until a catalogue location field exists
scientific_justification: Same catalogue-capability reasoning as the household-income group: classification should track what the catalogue can actually support.

exact_survey_question: Would you consider relocating to find different or better work? (Branch F)
why_classification_uncertain: Same catalogue-capability gap as willing_to_relocate.
alternative_classifications: INDIVIDUAL_CONTEXT_ONLY.
risk_if_allowed_to_drive_directly: Same as willing_to_relocate.
risk_if_prohibited_from_use: None currently.
recommended_classification: INDIVIDUAL_CONTEXT_ONLY (may_drive=False, may_support=True) until a catalogue location field exists
scientific_justification: Same reasoning as willing_to_relocate.

exact_survey_question: What is the highest level of education you have completed? (all branches)
current_classification: EDUCATION_AND_EXPERIENCE_CONTEXT (may_drive=True — flagged in the prior report as an explicit exception)
why_classification_uncertain: Completed-education level could legitimately gate NVQ-level or minimum-qualification course eligibility in principle, but the V2 course matching dataset has no documented entry-requirement or minimum-prior-qualification field for any of the 87 courses. The connecting rule does not currently exist on the catalogue side.
alternative_classifications: EDUCATION_AND_EXPERIENCE_CONTEXT with may_drive=False (explanation/context only) until a catalogue eligibility field is added.
risk_if_allowed_to_drive_directly: LLM invents an eligibility judgement ('you have the right qualification level for this NVQ course') that the catalogue cannot actually verify — a fabricated-eligibility risk, which is more serious than a mis-ranking because it looks like a factual gatekeeping claim.
risk_if_prohibited_from_use: A real, useful qualification-matching signal is left unused until the catalogue is extended — an acceptable, reversible trade-off.
recommended_classification: EDUCATION_AND_EXPERIENCE_CONTEXT, may_drive=False (reclassify the drive flag only) until a documented course entry-requirement field exists
scientific_justification: Directly matches the critical rule's requirement that the catalogue must provide the necessary information before a variable is allowed to drive a related decision.

exact_survey_question: How well does your current job use your actual qualifications and training? (Branch F)
current_classification: EDUCATION_AND_EXPERIENCE_CONTEXT (may_drive=True — flagged in the prior report as an explicit exception)
why_classification_uncertain: Measures a self-assessed match between the respondent's OWN qualifications and their CURRENT job — this is about their current employment quality, not about which NYSC course would suit them. On reflection this does not actually support course-ranking the way highest_edu_completed plausibly could.
alternative_classifications: EDUCATION_AND_EXPERIENCE_CONTEXT, may_drive=False (pure explanation/context).
risk_if_allowed_to_drive_directly: LLM could use a low qualification-job-match score to justify a specific course recommendation ('your quals are under-used, so you need training') without the respondent expressing that as a preference or intent.
risk_if_prohibited_from_use: None of substance — this variable does not map cleanly to any course attribute.
scientific_justification: On reflection this variable was over-classified in the original build; it describes current job quality, not training need, and should not have been marked as an exception alongside highest_edu_completed.

exact_survey_question: What has been the main obstacle in finding a good job? (Branch E)
why_classification_uncertain: A directly self-reported barrier, so it is not a pure proxy or inference — but the task's critical rule warns that 'employment insecurity must NOT automatically mean this person needs course X... programme content should still require relevant preference/interest/skill evidence.' The same logic applies to any stated barrier: it may legitimately support/contextualise a recommendation but must not, on its own, select programme CONTENT.
alternative_classifications: Keep as FEASIBILITY_OR_CONSTRAINT_CONTEXT, but the may_drive flag needs an explicit usage-scope restriction rather than a category change.
risk_if_allowed_to_drive_directly: If used to independently select programme CONTENT (e.g. 'obstacle = employers want higher quals' -> auto-recommend an NVQ course), it substitutes a barrier statement for actual interest/preference evidence.
risk_if_prohibited_from_use: A genuinely useful, directly-stated barrier is not available to help explain or prioritise recommendations at all — likely too conservative, since this is real first-person evidence, not a proxy.
recommended_classification: FEASIBILITY_OR_CONSTRAINT_CONTEXT retained, may_drive=True, but with an explicit documented usage-scope restriction: may adjust feasibility/prioritisation only, must never independently select programme field/content without corroborating DIRECT_PREFERENCE_OR_INTENT evidence
scientific_justification: This is genuine first-person evidence (unlike the household-role/income variables), so a category change is not warranted — the risk is entirely about scope of use, which needs an explicit rule at the scoring-design stage.

exact_survey_question: Looking back, what was the main obstacle you faced in finding this job? (Branch F)
why_classification_uncertain: Same reasoning as main_obstacle_finding_work, and additionally historical (describes a barrier to a job already obtained, not a live constraint).
alternative_classifications: Same as main_obstacle_finding_work; or EDUCATION_AND_EXPERIENCE_CONTEXT given its historical framing.
risk_if_allowed_to_drive_directly: Same content-substitution risk as main_obstacle_finding_work, compounded by describing a barrier that has already been resolved (they got the job).
risk_if_prohibited_from_use: Same as main_obstacle_finding_work.
recommended_classification: FEASIBILITY_OR_CONSTRAINT_CONTEXT retained, may_drive=True, with the same explicit usage-scope restriction as main_obstacle_finding_work
scientific_justification: Same reasoning as main_obstacle_finding_work; the historical framing further weakens (but does not eliminate) its relevance and should be reflected in explanation text as a past barrier, not a current one.

exact_survey_question: What is the most important challenge you face in running your business? (Branch F, conditional on employment_status = self-employed)
why_classification_uncertain: Same content-substitution risk as the other obstacle variables, applied to a small self-employed subgroup (n=14 of 90 applicable Branch F rows).
alternative_classifications: Same as main_obstacle_finding_work.
risk_if_allowed_to_drive_directly: Same content-substitution risk, with an added small-sample risk (n=14) of over-generalising from very few respondents.
risk_if_prohibited_from_use: Same as main_obstacle_finding_work.
recommended_classification: FEASIBILITY_OR_CONSTRAINT_CONTEXT retained, may_drive=True, with the same explicit usage-scope restriction, plus a small-sample caution note
scientific_justification: Same reasoning as main_obstacle_finding_work, with the added small-sample caveat already present in this variable's routing/missingness notes.

exact_survey_question: What is your main reason for not currently working or actively looking for work? (Branch G)
why_classification_uncertain: This is the core barrier variable for the entire inactive branch, so getting its usage scope right matters most here. It is directly self-reported (13-category reason), but the frozen clustering report itself explicitly warns that removing this variable reproduced the Branch G future-engagement clusters exactly (ARI 1.000) — i.e. it is descriptive of circumstance, not a driver of the profile system, and by the same logic should not be allowed to silently drive course-content selection either.
alternative_classifications: Same as main_obstacle_finding_work — keep the category, scope the usage.
risk_if_allowed_to_drive_directly: For inactive youth, this is the single highest-risk variable for content-substitution: e.g. 'reason = caring for family' could be auto-mapped to a specific course sector without any stated interest, which is precisely the prohibited pattern.
risk_if_prohibited_from_use: A very important explanatory fact for inactive youth becomes invisible to ranking entirely.
recommended_classification: FEASIBILITY_OR_CONSTRAINT_CONTEXT retained, may_drive=True, with the same explicit usage-scope restriction as the other obstacle variables, applied with extra caution given this is Branch G's single most consequential barrier field
scientific_justification: Genuine first-person evidence; the frozen report's own finding that this variable is descriptive rather than cluster-forming reinforces that it should inform explanation and feasibility framing, not silently select content.

exact_survey_question: What is your age? (all branches)
current_classification: INDIVIDUAL_CONTEXT_ONLY (may_drive=False) — already conservative, carried over from the prior report's §8
why_classification_uncertain: Already correctly scoped as non-driving, but included here because it was explicitly flagged for review in the prior report and matches the task's 'pay special attention' spirit (a demographic fact that is not quite the same as gender/parental-background but still carries proxy risk if courses ever gain an age-eligibility field).
alternative_classifications: PROTECTED_OR_PROXY_DO_NOT_USE if a reviewer judges age should be treated with the same caution as gender; or leave as INDIVIDUAL_CONTEXT_ONLY.
risk_if_allowed_to_drive_directly: None currently — already prohibited from driving.
risk_if_prohibited_from_use: None — no change proposed; recorded here for completeness and to close out the item raised in the prior report.
scientific_justification: Confirmed correct on review. Re-flag only if/when the course catalogue gains an explicit age-eligibility field, at which point this should move to a legitimate eligibility-driving role, not a proxy one.
